Heatmap of drugs (or organisations) by month

Source: R/plots.R
op_plot_heatmap.Rd

Tiles show each row's value relative to its own median (scale = "ratio"), which makes seasonality and trends comparable between drugs that differ a hundredfold in volume, or the raw value on a perceptually uniform colour scale (scale = "none").

Usage

op_plot_heatmap(
  data,
  y = NULL,
  row = NULL,
  date = "date",
  scale = c("ratio", "none"),
  order_by = c("mean", "peak", "name"),
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  source = TRUE,
  base_size = 8
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with a date column and a numeric column to plot.

y

Column to plot. Default "rate" if present, otherwise "items".

row

Column defining rows (default "ab_name", else "code").

date

Date column (default "date").

scale

"ratio" (default): colour is log2(value / row median) on a diverging scale centred at 1x, labelled as multiples. "none": raw value, sequential scale.

order_by

Row order: "mean" (largest on top, default), "peak" (month of maximum) or "name".

title, subtitle

Optional title (state the finding in a sentence) and subtitle.

source

Add the data-source caption (default TRUE); or a custom character string.

base_size

Base font size (default 8 pt, see theme_op()).

Value

A ggplot2::ggplot() object.

Examples

ex <- op_example[op_example$ab_name %in% c("Amoxicillin", "Nitrofurantoin", "Doxycycline",
                                           "Trimethoprim", "Flucloxacillin"), ]
op_plot_heatmap(ex, y = "items")
